speaker: Blue Arcadia
text: We welcome this project. It will help the port become more sustainable and contributes directly to SDG 9. But we do have concerns — and they are serious ones.

speaker: Blue Arcadia
text: If ships have to make a detour to reach our port, many will simply go to Babylonia's port instead. We risk losing our position as a global transport hub.

speaker: Blue Arcadia
text: A detour also negatively impacts SDGs 13 and 14: more fuel burned, more greenhouse gas emissions, more pollution of the marine environment. Arcadia would violate its UNCLOS obligations and worsen the very emissions this project is meant to reduce. That cannot be Arcadia's intention.

speaker: Legal Advisor
text: Arcadia has an obligation under Article 194 UNCLOS to prevent, reduce and control pollution of the marine environment. The International Tribunal for the Law of the Sea has held that anthropogenic GHG emissions into the atmosphere constitute marine pollution within the meaning of Article 1(1)(4) UNCLOS.

speaker: Legal Advisor
text: On the Paris Agreement: Arcadia has discretion as to how it reduces its GHG emissions, so long as the totality of its measures is ambitious and reflects its capacities.
